assembly_plan.proof_skeleton_nl: Define an explicit recursive family h_n inside the weighted polynomial ring. The decisive input is that polynomiality of Q_{A,B,d}(q) forces the specific quotient S/(h_{A+1},...,h_{A+d}) to be finite-dimensional. Since S is a positively graded polynomial ring of dimension d, any d homogeneous elements with Artinian quotient form a homogeneous regular sequence. Taking f_i=h_{A+i} then gives the required witnesses, and the standard Hilbert-series formula for a regular sequence yields exactly Q_{A,B,d}(q).

steps.derives: If d = 0, then the theorem holds: S=Q, Q_{A,B,0}(q)=1, and the empty sequence is a homogeneous regular sequence whose quotient has Hilbert series 1.
steps.trivial_justification: Lemma L5 gives exactly the d=0 case, including the empty sequence and the resulting Hilbert series.

steps.derives: Assume d > 0. For each i in {1,...,d}, the recursively defined element h_{A+i} lies in S and is homogeneous of weighted degree A+i.
steps.trivial_justification: Instantiate Lemma L1 with n=A+1, A+2, ..., A+d. Since A >= B >= 0, each A+i is nonnegative, so the lemma applies to every required index.

steps.derives: Assume d > 0. The quotient S/(h_{A+1},...,h_{A+d}) is finite-dimensional over Q.
steps.trivial_justification: This is the direct conclusion of Lemma L2 from the standing assumption that Q_{A,B,d}(q) belongs to Q[q].

steps.derives: Assume d > 0. The sequence h_{A+1},...,h_{A+d} is a homogeneous regular sequence in S; equivalently, for each i the image of h_{A+i} in S/(h_{A+1},...,h_{A+i-1}) is not a zero-divisor.
steps.trivial_justification: Step A2 provides homogeneity of the d elements and Step A3 provides finite-dimensionality of the quotient, so Lemma L3 applies directly.

steps.derives: Assume d > 0. Setting f_i := h_{A+i} for i=1,...,d gives homogeneous elements f_1,...,f_d in S with deg(f_i)=A+i, and for each i the image of f_i in S/(f_1,...,f_{i-1}) is not a zero-divisor.
steps.trivial_justification: This is immediate from the definition f_i := h_{A+i}, together with the degree information from Step A2 and the regular-sequence conclusion from Step A4.

steps.derives: Assume d > 0. The quotient by the constructed sequence satisfies Hilb_{S/(f_1,...,f_d)}(q) = prod_{i=1}^d (1-q^(A+i)) / prod_{i=1}^d (1-q^(B+i)) = Q_{A,B,d}(q).
steps.trivial_justification: Apply Lemma L4 with variable weights w_i=B+i and relation degrees e_i=A+i, then substitute the definition of Q_{A,B,d}(q).

steps.derives: For integers A, B, d with A >= B >= 0 and d >= 0, define Q_{A,B,d}(q) := prod_{i=1}^d (1 - q^(A+i)) / (1 - q^(B+i)), with the empty product equal to 1 when d = 0. Assume Q_{A,B,d}(q) belongs to Q[q]. Let S be the weighted polynomial ring Q[x_1, ..., x_d] graded by deg(x_i) = B+i; when d = 0 interpret S as Q. Then there exist homogeneous polynomials f_1, ..., f_d in S such that deg(f_i) = A+i for every i, and for each i the image of f_i in S/(f_1, ..., f_{i-1}) is not a zero-divisor. Equivalently, Q_{A,B,d}(q) is realized by a homogeneous regular sequence in a weighted polynomial ring with variable weights B+1, ..., B+d and relation degrees A+1, ..., A+d.

full_candidate.strategy_summary: Use a two-stage existence theorem. First translate polynomiality of Q_{A,B,d}(q) into divisibility inequalities via cyclotomic factor multiplicities, then into a Hall-type condition on which target degrees are visible on each coordinate subspace of the weighted affine space. Next invoke a weighted complete-intersection realization theorem: if every coordinate stratum sees enough accessible degrees, then one can choose homogeneous forms of the prescribed degrees whose only common zero is the origin.
